differences.what: the east range's eight windows glazed in small panes, a sunk panel under each, a sill course, a base course under the panels, a band over the heads and a cornice line under the coping; the windows narrower than built and set closer to the lodge, with a broad pier at the round end
differences.how: T-3164: pale panes under dark sash bars (4 x 3), a moulded panel 1.85-3.25 m, courses at 1.6, 3.3, 4.65 and 5.4 m, windows 1.25 m from 3.5 to 4.65 m respaced from 0.15 m at the lodge to a 1.0 m pier at the round end; their places fall within about 3 px of the plate's. The overcast render draws no relief, so the courses and panels show only in the app's sun

differences.what: the lodge: a two-storey stone building, a tall ground storey with a loggia of three openings under an entablature, a balcony band, one small upper sash, and a steep hipped roof to a flat deck inside an iron cresting
differences.how: T-3164: rebuilt from the draft's brick block (eave 7.1 m, plain hip, stack on the north-west) to the plate's: stone, storeys of 5.5 and 2.7 m (eave 8.2 m), openings at 0.51, 1.65 and 3.35 m, the band at 5.3-5.9 m, the deck 3.7 m over the eave with its cresting; eave, deck, band and openings fall within about 5 px of the plate's. Lowe's print also shows one stack behind the east slope, where the record now stands it

differences.what: the upright glass round the transept's arms between the podium and the springing reads as dark lights in pale frames
differences.how: T-3164: dark panes in 0.12 m pale frames at 0.85 m, with sill, transom and head bars, on each arm's end and sides (it was the roof's pale substitute glass, unframed)

differences.what: the conservatory's pointed nave, frame, podium, entrance, transept, drum and dome, as in the plate
differences.how: T-3179, built to the plate; through this diagnostic camera they fall within about 20 px of the print

differences.what: the east range's masonry face with its eight windows, and the domed colonnade at its round end
the far range's coping falls about 14 px (0.6 m) above the print's and the lodge about 30 px west of it
differences.how: T-3153: two camera fits disagree; the print is cropped and its fit is one of a family (the solve), and the uncropped plate puts the coping within 5 px

differences.what: the transept's east end, a narrow upright edge in the print
differences.how: as the plate's record: the sheet's arm plan is held

differences.what: the north front's band between the podium and the springing: round-headed lights in white framing, four each side of the entrance, and three along the east flank north of the transept
differences.how: T-3164: each light a round-headed pane in the planted shade behind the glass, in white framing under a top rail

differences.what: the north front's arched glass reads dark over the planted interior, its white bars over it and the roof's light above, not as an opaque pale gable
differences.how: T-3164: the conservatory's depth drawn in shade inside the nave to about 5.2 m

differences.what: the transept arms' lights have round heads and tracery (drawn square-headed); the podium is rusticated and panelled; the range's pilasters and the colonnade's columns heavier than built
differences.how: T-3153: heights, places and outlines agree within about 0.3 m; the difference is relief and openwork under the bar, drawn as plain lights, ashlar and octagonal shafts Reopened 2026-10-28 on the owner's report ("still way off from a photographic match"): under T-3153 an element missing or the wrong shape, or a gap over about 0.3 m, is open, never within tolerance. T-3164: the range's panels, sill and base courses are now built; the band's arched heads and tracery, the podium's rustication and the heavier pilasters and columns are not.

differences.what: a light iron cresting along the transept's level crest from its hipped end to the nave, a finial over the transept's end and a small ornament over the nave's apex (T-3164)
iron cresting along the east range's coping (the transept's is built; the range's is not yet)

the nave's arch is a smooth curve (the render's was four planar facets a half): now eight a half, the chord inside the arc at most 0.02 m, and the transept's section and the dome drawn as smoothly; the arch reads as one curve from 18th Street (T-3164)
the glass reads pale (the sky in it) on the transept, the drum and the domes
differences.how: T-3179: those parts, which stand outside the nave's one transparent envelope, take an opaque glazing toned pale (glass_sky) instead of the kit's dark substitute; colour itself is not shown (a monochrome picture)

differences.what: the north range: the picture shows garden and the lodge's front where the 1911 sheet draws a 23.7 m glass range from the conservatory's south end to the lodge, with only a short low curved glass link beside the conservatory
differences.how: the picture is of 1894-97 and cannot show 1904: the range was lengthened between about 1897 and 1911 and nothing dates it inside that span, so the 1904 record keeps the sheet's range (L-pullman-conservatory-3179). Its north end, which the picture does show, is built to it: a low curved glass roof, eave about 1.9 m, crown about 4.2 m

differences.what: the glasshouses' south and west sides and the ranges' roofs behind their parapets
differences.how: the camera stands north-east of them; the sheet's glass roof is built low behind the parapet

differences.what: the lodge shows no east face or east slope over the east range's coping (sky and a railing there), where the render, on the 1911 sheet's 11.6 m-deep two-storey outline, stands its east face and slope
differences.how: T-3164: unresolved between the sheet's plan and the two solved cameras, which both stand east of the lodge; either the two-storey block was shallower in 1894-97 (the north range was lengthened between about 1897 and 1911, and the lodge may have been too) or the cameras stand further west than solved. Not read yet, so open.

differences.what: the lodge's bowed north-east corner with the flared eave over it, the balcony's curved front and balustrade, round columns in the loggia, finials at the deck's corners, and the lower hipped roof over the front's west part
differences.how: T-3164: the draft builder draws the loggia as dark openings between square piers and a flat banded balcony; the bow, the balcony's curve and the second roof are not built

differences.what: the dome and its drum stand about 25 px (0.6 m) west of the plate's (Lowe shows the same, about 20 px)

differences.what: the gate piers with their scroll wings, the walks, the lawns, the standard trees, the shrubs and the street trees

differences.what: the owner's report, 2026-10-28: the greenhouse ground south of 18th Street is way off the photograph; the long range renders as a blank wall with square holes and the lodge in red brick, where the print shows a glazed range on a stone base and a stone lodge, and the pavilion's great arched glass front renders as an opaque gable over a black opening
differences.how: the range glazed and the lodge in stone (T-3164, #1429); the north front's glass reads dark over its planted interior with its white bars, over a band of round-headed lights, the entrance in its stone surround (T-3164)

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
